facts.f: Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
facts.e: Only Mercury and Venus are closer to the Sun.

facts.f: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water.
facts.e: Most of it is salty ocean water. That is why Earth looks blue from space.

facts.f: Earth has layers like an onion: crust, mantle, outer core and inner core.
facts.e: We live on the thin, rocky crust. The core at the centre is mostly iron and nickel.

facts.f: Earth's inner core is solid, even though it is extremely hot.
facts.e: The pressure at the centre is so enormous that the metal is squeezed solid.

facts.f: Earth spins once on its axis in about 24 hours.
facts.e: This spinning gives us day and night. The side facing the Sun has day.

facts.f: Earth's axis is tilted by about 23.5 degrees.
facts.e: This tilt is the reason we have seasons.

facts.f: Seasons are caused by Earth's tilt, not by its distance from the Sun.
facts.e: In fact, Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, during winter in India.

facts.f: There are seven continents.
facts.e: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

facts.f: Asia is the largest continent.
facts.e: It has the most land and the most people of any continent.

facts.f: Australia is the smallest continent.
facts.e: It is called the island continent because it is surrounded by water.

facts.f: The Equator divides Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
facts.e: It is an imaginary line around the middle of Earth at 0 degrees latitude.

facts.f: Lines of latitude run east to west. Lines of longitude run from pole to pole.
facts.e: Together they make a grid that helps us find any place on Earth.

facts.f: The Prime Meridian, at 0 degrees longitude, passes through Greenwich in London.
facts.e: Times around the world are measured from this line.

facts.f: The air is about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen.
facts.e: The last 1% is mostly argon, with tiny amounts of carbon dioxide and other gases.

facts.f: The ozone layer protects us from the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays.
facts.e: It is a layer of ozone gas high up in the stratosphere.

facts.f: Melted rock is called magma underground and lava once it comes out.
facts.e: A volcano is an opening in Earth's crust where lava, ash and gas escape.

facts.f: Earthquakes happen when huge pieces of Earth's crust suddenly move.
facts.e: These giant pieces are called tectonic plates. They slowly push, pull and slide past each other.

facts.f: The Himalayas are still slowly rising.
facts.e: The Indian plate keeps pushing into the Eurasian plate, squeezing the mountains upwards.

facts.f: There are three main types of rock: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.
facts.e: Igneous rock forms from cooled magma, sedimentary from layers of sand and mud, and metamorphic when rock is changed by heat and pressure.

facts.f: Fossils are usually found in sedimentary rocks.
facts.e: Plants and animals got buried in layers of mud and sand that slowly turned into rock.

facts.f: Diamonds are made of carbon.
facts.e: They form deep underground, where great heat and pressure squeeze carbon into crystals.

facts.f: Water keeps moving in a cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.
facts.e: The Sun heats water into vapour, it cools into clouds, falls as rain, and gathers in rivers and seas.

facts.f: Clouds are made of tiny water droplets or ice crystals.
facts.e: Water vapour itself is invisible. We see clouds when the vapour cools into droplets.

facts.f: A lightning bolt is several times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
facts.e: Lightning can heat the air to about 30,000 degrees Celsius for a split second.

facts.f: We see lightning before we hear thunder.
facts.e: Light travels much faster than sound, so the flash reaches us first.

facts.f: A rainbow forms when sunlight passes through raindrops.
facts.e: The drops split white sunlight into its colours: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red.

facts.f: Glaciers are huge rivers of ice that move very slowly.
facts.e: They form where more snow falls each year than melts, and the snow is pressed into ice.

facts.f: The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert in the world.
facts.e: It is almost as big as the whole of the United States.

facts.f: Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth.
facts.e: A desert is a place with very little rain or snow. Antarctica is very cold and very dry.

facts.f: New soil forms very slowly.
facts.e: It can take hundreds of years for nature to make just a few centimetres of soil from rock.

facts.f: Earth is not a perfect ball. It bulges a little at the Equator.
facts.e: Earth's spinning pushes the middle outwards slightly.

facts.f: The distance around Earth at the Equator is about 40,000 km.
facts.e: Driving that far without stopping at 100 km per hour would take more than 16 days.

facts.f: Earth is about 4.5 billion years old.
facts.e: Scientists worked this out by studying very old rocks and meteorites.

facts.f: Earth acts like a giant magnet.
facts.e: That is why a compass needle points north.

facts.f: The Northern and Southern Lights are called auroras.
facts.e: They glow when tiny particles from the Sun crash into gases high in the air near the poles.

facts.f: Monsoon winds bring most of India's rain.
facts.e: Most of the rain falls between June and September.

facts.f: Hot air rises because it is lighter than the cool air around it.
facts.e: Warm air is less dense, so it floats upwards. Hot-air balloons use this idea.

facts.f: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth.
facts.e: Monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal hit the Khasi Hills and pour down huge amounts of rain.

facts.f: A tsunami is a series of giant sea waves.
facts.e: Tsunamis are usually caused by an earthquake under the sea.

facts.f: The Ring of Fire is a horseshoe-shaped belt around the Pacific Ocean.
facts.e: It has many volcanoes and earthquakes because several tectonic plates meet there.

facts.f: Ice floats on water.
facts.e: When water freezes it expands, so ice is less dense than liquid water.

facts.f: Weather is what the air is like today. Climate is the usual pattern over many years.
facts.e: Scientists usually look at about 30 years of weather to describe a place's climate.

quiz.q: Which planet from the Sun is Earth?
quiz.x: Mercury is first, Venus second and Earth third.

quiz.q: About how much of Earth's surface is covered by water?
quiz.x: Roughly seven-tenths of Earth's surface is water, mostly ocean.

quiz.q: What causes the seasons on Earth?
o: Earth getting closer to the Sun
quiz.x: Because Earth is tilted, each hemisphere gets more direct sunlight at different times of the year.

quiz.q: Which is the largest continent?
quiz.x: Asia has the most land and the most people.

quiz.q: Which is the smallest continent?
quiz.x: Australia is the smallest continent.

quiz.q: Which gas makes up most of the air?
quiz.x: Air is about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen.

quiz.q: Which layer protects us from the Sun's ultraviolet rays?
quiz.x: Ozone high in the stratosphere absorbs most harmful ultraviolet rays.

quiz.q: What do we call melted rock that comes out of a volcano?
quiz.x: Under the ground it is called magma. Once it comes out, it is called lava.

quiz.q: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
quiz.x: Lightning and thunder happen together, but light reaches us almost at once while sound takes longer.

quiz.q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
quiz.x: The Sahara covers much of northern Africa. The Gobi is a cold desert.

quiz.q: What is the Prime Meridian?
o: The line around the South Pole
The 0 degree longitude line through Greenwich
quiz.x: Longitude is measured east and west from the Prime Meridian at Greenwich, London.

quiz.q: How many continents are there?
quiz.x: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

quiz.q: What are diamonds made of?
quiz.x: Diamonds are carbon crystals formed under great heat and pressure.

quiz.q: What brings most of India's rain?
quiz.x: The south-west monsoon brings most rain from June to September.

quiz.q: Which type of rock forms when lava or magma cools?
quiz.x: 'Igneous' comes from the Latin word for fire.

quiz.q: What is Earth's inner core like?
quiz.x: The inner core is mostly iron and nickel, kept solid by enormous pressure.

quiz.q: How many colours do we usually name in a rainbow?
quiz.x: Violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red: VIBGYOR.

quiz.q: What usually causes a tsunami?
quiz.x: A sudden movement of the sea floor pushes up a huge amount of water.

quiz.q: Why does ice float on water?
o: Ice is less dense than liquid water
quiz.x: Water expands when it freezes, so a block of ice weighs less than the same space of water.

quiz.q: About how old is Earth?
quiz.x: Scientists dated Earth's age from rocks and meteorites.

quiz.q: What does the Equator divide Earth into?
quiz.x: The Equator runs around the middle of Earth at 0 degrees latitude.
